newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's TMM says to issue $200 mln note.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's TMM says to issue $200 mln note.

text.p: Mexican shipping and transportation company, Transportacion Maritima Mexicana SA de CV will issue a $200 million senior note due in 2006 within the next month, director of investor relations Pedro Mejorada told Reuters on Monday.
"We are starting the road show next week. We hope to have it placed within the next month," he said.
The income from the note will be used for corporate purposes and to help pay down an outstanding note that comes due in late 1997.
"Part of the proceeds will be used for payment of an outstanding medium-term note worth $75 million that comes due next year," he said.
The company expects to place the 2006 senior note with institutional investors in the United States, he said.
Standard & Poor's on Monday assigned a BB rating to the upcoming senior note issue.

S&P's also raised the ratings on the company's outstanding senior unsecured notes due 2000 and 2003 to BB from BB-minus, due to an ongoing reduction in secured debt as a proportion of the capital structure, it said.
Standard and Poor's said that at the same time it has affirmed the company's BB corporate credit rating.
The credit rating agency said TMM's credit outlook is stable.
TMM is one of a number of Mexican companies looking to refinance corporate debt early, as Mexico benefits from favorable investor sentiment.
S&P said most of the TMM's debt is denominated in U.S. dollars, however, and with about 95 percent of total revenues also denominated in dollars, the company has a natural hedge.
TMM has a leading position in Mexico's container shipping industry.
